settings.title: Settings
settings.addressPlaceholder: https://ha.example.com (empty = same address as this page)
settings.tokenHelp: Create a token in Home Assistant under your profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens. It is stored in this browser only.
settings.needToken: Enter a token to connect to Home Assistant.
settings.source.mock: Showing test data. Log in to Home Assistant in this browser (tick “Keep me logged in”), or paste a token below.
settings.source.token: Connected to Home Assistant with a saved token.
settings.source.login: Connected with this browser’s Home Assistant login.
editor.title: Placement mode
editor.draftNotice: Showing an unsaved draft from this browser. Copy site.json to keep it.
editor.autoIn: {area} · placed automatically, tap to set its spot
editor.noEntities: No entities found. Connect to Home Assistant to list all of them.
editor.missingNone: Every device in site.json exists in Home Assistant.
editor.missingHelp: Used in: {where}. Remove it, or tap a spot to place it again if it comes back.
editor.missingLeft: {name} removed from rooms and lists. Change {where} in the setup guide or in site.json.
editor.pickFirst: Pick something in the list first, or drag a lamp to move it.
editor.tapWhere: Tap the room on the floor plan.
editor.tapWhereLight: Tap where it is: on the floor plan for indoor, on the overview for outdoor. Tap again for more fixtures outdoors.
editor.outsideRooms: That spot is outside every room. Tap inside a room.
editor.onlyLightsOutdoor: Only lights and switches can be placed on the overview.
editor.drawHelp: Click the corners in order. Copy the list into site.json as area, outline or a panel.
editor.drawPrompt: Click corners on the overview or the floor plan.
editor.copiedJson: site.json copied. Paste it over the file in sites/<site>/.
editor.updating: Fetching the latest version from GitHub…
editor.updatedRestart: Installed version {commit}. Restart Home Assistant to finish.
editor.picked: {name} selected. Drag it to move it, or tap a new spot.
report.title: Report a problem
report.intro: This opens a new issue on GitHub with the text below filled in. It holds versions, browser, screen and counts, never the names of your rooms, devices or pictures. Issues are public: read it first, and change it if you like.
report.copyManual: Copy the selected text by hand.
report.diagnostics: If you are an administrator, attach diagnostics as well: Settings → Devices & services → SmartHomeDash → ⋮ → Download diagnostics. The file holds counts and sizes only.
report.questionsHelp: Questions, wishes and pictures of your own dashboard are welcome in Discussions, where others can answer and vote.
app.emptyAdmin: Start the setup guide to add a picture of your home, floor plans and your lights.
app.emptyUser: An administrator needs to set up this dashboard first.
setup.title: Setup
setup.overviewIntroApartment: Optional. Without an overview picture the dashboard opens on the floor plan, which suits an apartment. Upload a picture from above to show the building with live lights instead.
setup.removeOverviewHelp: Show only the floor plans, for example for an apartment. Buildings, windows, solar panels and outdoor lights drawn on the picture are removed.
setup.welcomeApartment: Welcome! The dashboard starts with an example floor plan. Replace it with your own under Floor plans, or keep it and go straight to Lights and heating to place your lights and thermostats.
setup.basicsIntro: Name the dashboard and pick the language shown on screen.
setup.welcome: Welcome! The dashboard starts with an example house. Replace its pictures with your own home under Overview picture and Floor plans, or keep them and go straight to Lights and heating to place your own lights and thermostats.
setup.quickHelp: Makes a floor plan for each floor in Home Assistant, with a tile for each of its areas ({n} in all). Lights, thermostats and temperature sensors show up in their rooms by themselves. Nothing to draw: you can add pictures and draw the rooms later.
setup.quickNothing: Every area is already on a floor plan.
setup.quickDone: Made {plans} floor plans with {rooms} rooms. Save to see them.
setup.planTiles: Made from Home Assistant: a tile per area. Upload a picture of the plan to draw the rooms where they are.
setup.uploadPlanPicture: Upload a picture of the plan
setup.redrawNote: Draw each room on the picture. Its link to the Home Assistant area is kept, and so are its lights.
setup.exampleOverview: These are the example pictures. Upload your own day picture to replace them; the example buildings, windows and solar panels then need to be drawn again on your picture.
setup.examplePlans: The example floor plans are shown below. Remove them and upload your own, or keep them and link each room to one of your Home Assistant areas.
setup.name: Name
setup.languageHelp: Room and light names are shown as you write them.
setup.overviewIntro: A picture of the property seen from above, for example a drone photo. Lights glow on it, solar panels light up green, and tapping a building opens its floor plan.
setup.nightHelp: Shown after sunset. Same size and framing as the day picture, with every light off.
setup.nightSizeMismatch: The evening picture must be {w} × {h} pixels like the day picture; this one is {w2} × {h2}.
setup.checkNight: The day picture changed. Check that the evening picture still has the same size and framing.
setup.uploaded: Picture uploaded. Save to keep the change.
setup.notAPicture: That file is not a picture.
setup.buildingsHelp: Outline each building and pick its Home Assistant area. A building with a floor plan lifts its roof when tapped; one without, such as a shed, opens the lights, heating and sensors of its area.
setup.noPlansYet: Add a floor plan in the next step, then pick it here or there.
setup.solarHelp: Outline each panel area. They glow green while producing, stronger towards the peak output. Pick the solar power sensor under Energy.
setup.windowsHelp: Outline windows and pick the room behind them. They light up when a light in that room is on.
setup.windowsNeedRooms: Add a floor plan with rooms first; windows light up from the lights in their room.
setup.outdoorLightsHint: Outdoor lights are placed on the picture in the last step, Lights and heating.
setup.plansIntro: Upload a picture of each floor plan: a drawing, a scan or a realistic render seen from above. Then outline the rooms on it, and pick the building on the overview picture that opens it: tapping the building lifts its roof.
setup.planNoPicture: This floor plan has no picture.
setup.addPlanHelp: One per building or storey. The picture should be cropped to the outer walls.
setup.noDrone: No drone? Make the pictures from a map
setup.noDroneIntro: A 3D map and an AI image model (ChatGPT, Gemini or similar) give a day and an evening picture that fit the dashboard, in about 15 minutes.
setup.noDrone1: Find your home in a map with 3D view: Google Earth, Google Maps (satellite, Globe view) or Apple Maps. Tilt about 45°, turn the entrance side towards you, zoom until the property fills the screen and hide labels.
setup.noDrone2: Take a screenshot and crop it to the property in landscape, at least 1200 pixels wide.
setup.noDrone3: Upload the screenshot to the image model with the day prompt. Check that the buildings are the same and no lamps are lit; ask for corrections in the same chat if needed.
setup.noDrone4: Upload the day picture you made (not the screenshot) with the evening prompt.
setup.noDrone5: Upload both pictures above. They must have exactly the same size; scale the evening picture if the model changed it.
setup.noDroneNote: Every light must be off in both pictures: the dashboard draws the light itself. Map imagery belongs to the map provider, so keep the result for your own dashboard.
setup.noDroneMore: Full guide, with a variant for satellite views and facade photos
setup.copyManual: Could not copy: select the text and copy it.
setup.energyFlowHelp: Lines on the picture show where the power goes: from the sun, the battery and the grid to the house, the car, the battery or the grid, in the colour of the source, wider and faster with more power. Tap where each one is; the house and the grid have a sensible default, the battery and charger are only drawn once placed.
setup.pointHelp: Tap the spot on the picture.
setup.areasHelp: Pick the Home Assistant area for each room. The room takes the area's name and its lights, thermostat and temperature sensor; place the lights where they are afterwards.
setup.matchAreasHelp: Rooms named like one of your Home Assistant areas, and floor plans named like a floor, can be linked in one go.
setup.matchAreas: Link rooms and floors with the same name
setup.noAreaMatch: No room has the same name as an area. Pick an area for each room below.
setup.energyIntro: Pick the sensors for the energy cards. Leave anything you do not have empty; its card or row is hidden.
setup.directionHelp: Inverters count power in different directions. Compare with the app or display of your inverter: if the battery is shown as charging while it is giving power to the house, or buying while you are selling, tick the box to turn it around.
setup.priceHelp: A price sensor with prices for today, per hour or per quarter-hour, such as Nord Pool.
setup.heatDevicesHelp: Thermostats that are not in a room, such as a heat pump, shown in the heating card. Room thermostats are linked in the last step.
setup.buttonsIntro: Pick scenes and scripts to show as buttons, and name them.
setup.noScenes: No scenes or scripts found in Home Assistant.
setup.allLightsShow: Show the All on and All off buttons (in the lights card and the header)
setup.allLightsIntro: Lights that are not ticked are left alone, such as garden lights on a schedule.
setup.allLightsNone: No lights on the dashboard yet.
setup.goodnightIntro: The lights stay as they are for a few minutes, then the same lights as All off turn off. The countdown runs in Home Assistant and shows on every screen.
setup.goodnightThenHelp: For example to lock up, turn the TV off or lower the heating.
setup.wallIntro: For tablets and screens on the wall: the doorbell camera, idle mode and light mode. All of it is optional.
setup.doorbellHelp: When the doorbell rings, every open dashboard shows the camera in a window that closes by itself.
setup.doorbellEntity: Doorbell (rings when it turns on or fires)
setup.idleHelp: Only on screens in kiosk mode. After a while without touch the dashboard goes back to the start and closes open panels.
setup.dimHelp: Between these times the screen dims when nobody touches it. A touch wakes it without pressing anything.
setup.wake: Motion sensors that wake the screen
setup.noMotion: No motion or presence sensors found in Home Assistant.
setup.liteHelp: No blur, blending or animation, for older tablets that stutter. For one screen only, use the Kiosk mode button on that screen, or add ?lite to its address.
wall.title: Wall screen
wall.kioskHelp: Kiosk mode shows only the dashboard, full screen. Hold the clock for two seconds to leave it.
wall.liteHelp: For older tablets: no blur, blending or animation, so the dashboard stays quick. Auto turns it on for slow devices, or for every screen when the setup guide says so.
wall.doorbellOn: When the doorbell rings, the camera opens in a window that closes by itself. The test shows the window on this screen only.
wall.doorbellOff: Not set up. Pick the doorbell and its camera in the setup guide, under Wall screen.
backup.intro: Download this dashboard as one file to keep a copy or move it to another Home Assistant, bring one back in, or go back to an earlier saved version.
backup.unsaved: You have unsaved changes in the guide. Importing or restoring restarts the dashboard, and they are lost.
backup.exportHelp: A .zip with site.json and every picture. Entity ids come along, so keep it to yourself.
backup.importHelp: Choose a .zip exported from SmartHomeDash. It replaces this dashboard's settings and adds its pictures. The settings you have now are kept as a restore point below.
backup.versionsHelp: The last 10 saved versions of the settings, newest first. Pictures are not part of a restore point.
backup.noVersions: No earlier versions yet. One is kept each time you save.
backup.restored: Restored the version from {when}. Restarting the dashboard …
setup.lightsIntro: Lights, switches, thermostats and temperature sensors are placed by tapping where they are.
setup.lightsStep1: Pick an entity in the list.
setup.lightsStep2: Tap where it is: in a room on the floor plan, or on the overview picture for outdoor lights. Thermostats and sensors are linked to the room you tap.
setup.lightsStep3: Save to Home Assistant when done.
setup.lightsNeedPictures: Add an overview picture or a floor plan first.
setup.drawHelp: Click the corners in order. At least three corners.
shape.help: Drag a corner to move it. Drag the small dot on an edge to add a corner. Press and hold a corner (or right-click it) to remove it. Drag inside the shape to move all of it. Arrow keys nudge the selected corner or the shape, Shift moves further.
shape.minCorners: A shape needs at least three corners.
card.description: Your home as a picture: the overview, a floor plan or a room of a SmartHomeDash dashboard.
card.noSite: Choose a dashboard for this card.
card.editor.heightHelp: Leave empty in a sections view, where you resize the card in the grid.
